title: CPA Phone Outreach Strategy
summary: Phone outreach strategy for CPAs after 51 cold emails yielded 0 replies.
content:
CPA Phone Outreach Strategy

Built: 2026-03-12 | Agent: Jacob | For: Patrik making the calls

Council says phone > email for first AI advisory client. 51 emails, 0 replies. Time to pick up the phone.

Why Phone Works for CPAs

  • CPAs are drowning in email during tax season. Phone cuts through.
  • A real voice is harder to ignore than another cold email in a full inbox.
  • CPAs are relationship people. Voice builds trust faster than text.
  • You're not selling. You're one business owner calling another to talk shop.

The Script (30-Second Opener)

This is a conversation starter, not a pitch. Patrik's voice. Casual, direct, human.

If they answer:

"Hey [First name], this is Patrik from Ahead of Market. I know you're deep in tax season so I'll be quick.

I run a small creative and tech studio here in Phoenix. I've been building AI systems for my own business, automating the stuff that used to eat my whole day, and I keep hearing from CPAs that they're buried in the same kind of repetitive work.

I'm not trying to sell you anything. I'm genuinely curious if that's something you've thought about at all. Even just a 15-minute call after April 15 when you come up for air."

If they engage (transition lines):

Pick whichever fits the conversation. Don't use all of them.

  • "Honestly, I built this system because I was tired of spending hours triaging emails and follow-ups. It handles that for me now. I started wondering if it could work for firms like yours."
  • "The way I see it, CPAs are doing a ton of high-value thinking work but spending half their day on admin that could be automated. That's the gap I'm looking at."
  • "I'm not an accountant, so I'd love to just learn about your workflow. What takes the most time that doesn't actually require your expertise?"
  • "After April 15, when things calm down, I'd love to do a quick 30-minute scan of your operations. No charge, no pitch. I just want to see if what I built could apply."

Closing (if there's interest):

"Cool. What works better for you, a quick call the week of April 21st, or would grabbing coffee somewhere in [their area] be easier? I'll send you a quick email so you have my info."

Closing (if they're not interested right now):

"Totally get it. Can I shoot you an email so you have my info in case it ever comes up? No pressure at all."

If they push back or say no:

"No worries at all. Figured it was worth a shot. Have a good rest of tax season."

Keep it clean. No convincing, no objection-handling. If they say no, thank them and move on. Patrik's reputation > one lead.

Voicemail Script (Under 20 Seconds)

They won't call back from a voicemail alone. The goal is name recognition so when the follow-up email arrives, it's not completely cold.

"Hey [First name], this is Patrik from Ahead of Market in Phoenix. I work with a few businesses on their AI operations and wanted to see if that's something you've thought about. No rush at all. I'll shoot you an email. Have a good one."

That's it. No phone number (they'll see it on caller ID). No long pitch. Short enough they actually listen to the whole thing.

Target List: Top 10 CPAs to Call This Week

Prioritized by: construction specialization (warm intro angle), firm size (smaller = reach the decision maker), and prior contact status.

ALREADY EMAILED (follow up by phone)

# Firm Contact Phone Notes
1 Foster Financial CPA Nick T. Foster fosterfinancialcpa.com (find direct line) Emailed Mar 12. ALL-IN on construction. Worked for CORE Construction, Kinkaid Civil, etc. Best fit in the entire pipeline.
2 BeachFleischman CPAs Bryan S. Eto (construction principal) beachfleischman.com main line, ask for Bryan Emailed Mar 12. CCIFP-certified. Top 200 firm. Bigger = more referrals if you get in.

NEW TARGETS (from partnership strategy, not yet contacted)

# Firm Contact Phone Notes
3 Sean Core CPA Sean Core (founder) seancorecpa.com (find direct line) Small firm, dedicated contractor/construction practice. Easiest decision-maker access.
4 Conover Asay CPAs Construction practice partner conoverasay.com Full construction accounting page. Serves GCs, subs, construction management.
5 Wallace Plese + Dreher Construction practice lead wpdcpa.com Mid-size, dedicated construction vertical. Certified QuickBooks ProAdvisors for contractors.
6 Price Kong Construction Services Group head pricekong.com Larger firm. Construction Services Group with "extensive experience." More clients = more referrals.

AI ADVISORY TARGETS (CPAs without construction specialty)

# Firm Contact Phone Notes
7 Henry+Horne Managing partner hhcpa.com Top AZ firm. Multiple industries. Large enough to have real operational pain.
8 Eide Bailly Phoenix office managing partner eidebailly.com National firm with Phoenix presence. Tech-forward reputation. More likely to be interested in AI.
9 Fester & Chapman Partner festerchapman.com Small Phoenix firm. Easier to reach decision maker. Generalist = operational AI pitch.
10 BeachFleischman (2nd contact) Christopher A. Lutes (Managing Principal, Phoenix) beachfleischman.com If Bryan Eto doesn't bite, go to the managing principal. Different angle: firm-wide operations, not just construction practice.

Before calling: Google each firm. Find direct lines on their website, LinkedIn, or Google Maps listing. Many CPA firms list partner direct lines or extensions.

Call Cadence

Daily Volume

  • 3-5 calls per day. Not 20. This is Patrik calling, not a call center.
  • Best window: Tuesday through Thursday, 10:00-11:30 AM or 2:00-3:30 PM. CPAs are less likely to be in client meetings during these windows. Avoid Monday (worst day in tax season) and Friday afternoon (checked out).
  • Block 30 minutes. That's enough for 3-5 dials including voicemails.

Weekly Plan

Day Calls Who
Tue 3-4 calls Foster Financial, BeachFleischman (Bryan Eto), Sean Core CPA
Wed 3-4 calls Conover Asay, Wallace Plese + Dreher, Price Kong
Thu 3-4 calls Henry+Horne, Eide Bailly, Fester & Chapman, BeachFleischman (Lutes)

Follow-Up After Each Call

Outcome Next Step Timing
Connected, they're interested Send email with Patrik's info. Book the post-April 15 call on the spot. Add to calendar. Same day
Connected, not interested Thank them. Log it. Move on. No follow-up. Done
Connected, "call me after tax season" "Absolutely. I'll reach out the week of April 21." Set a calendar reminder. Send a brief email so they have your info. April 21 week
Voicemail Send follow-up email within 1 hour referencing the voicemail. Same day
No answer, no voicemail Try once more the next day at a different time. If no answer again, send email only. Next day
Gatekeeper "Hey, I was hoping to reach [name]. I run a tech studio in Phoenix and wanted to ask them a quick question about how they're handling operations. Is there a good time to catch them?" Be friendly. Don't over-explain. Per their suggestion

Follow-Up Email (After Voicemail or Call)

Subject: quick voicemail from Patrik

[First name], just left you a quick voicemail. I run a small studio in Phoenix and I've been building AI systems that automate a lot of the repetitive business operations stuff.

I know you're deep in tax season. After April 15 when things settle down, I'd love to grab 15 minutes and show you what I built. No pitch, just curious if any of it applies to your world.

If you ever want to talk shop, I'm around.

{DEFAULT GMAIL SIGNATURE}

Timing Strategy

Right Now (March 12 - April 15): Plant Seeds

CPAs are heads-down in tax season. They won't have a 30-minute call this week. That's fine. The goal right now is:

  1. Make the call. Leave the voicemail. Send the email.
  2. Get on their radar so "Patrik from Ahead of Market" is a name they recognize.
  3. Book the post-tax-season conversation for the week of April 21.

April 21 - May 9: Harvest

This is the real window. CPAs just survived tax season. They're catching their breath, thinking about what went wrong, and open to "how do I make next year less painful." This is when the 30-minute quick scan happens. This is when the $2,500 audit gets pitched.

The Ask (for now):

"15 minutes after April 15" is the only thing Patrik is asking for. Not a sale. Not a demo. A conversation. The sale happens on that call when Patrik runs the quick scan and they see the gaps.

Key Reminders

  • You're Patrik, not a sales rep. Business owner to business owner. Two people who run companies in Phoenix.
  • Don't pitch on the first call. The goal is the post-April 15 meeting, not a close.
  • AI is the hook, not the product. "I built this thing for my own business" is more interesting than "we sell AI audits."
  • Construction CPAs are the priority. Foster Financial and Sean Core CPA are the #1 and #2 calls. They already serve your exact target market.
  • 3 calls a day is enough. Quality over volume. One good conversation > 20 voicemails.
  • Log everything. After each call, tell Jacob the outcome. Jacob updates cold-outreach-log.md and sets follow-up reminders.

This strategy is for Patrik's calls only. Jacob does not make calls or send emails. Jacob researches, prepares targets, and logs results after Patrik reports back.
